offices.label: Office of Student Affairs and Financial Aid
offices.tagline: Overseeing student life, discipline, and scholarships to support holistic student development.

items.heading: Purpose
items.body: The Office of Student Affairs and Financial Aid (OSAFA) aims to empower students by upholding the University core values: Mabuti, Magaling, and May Malasakit sa Kapwa. It oversees all the co- and extracurricular activities of the students on and off-campus. It also facilitates student leadership formation. It supports maintaining discipline and proper decorum among the students and recommends appropriate disciplinary measures when necessary. It also handles scholarship grants and other financial aid given to deserving students.

items.heading: Our Services
items.body: To achieve the total development of students, the office primarily aims to facilitate student formation through various opportunities and relevant activities that are geared towards fostering personal growth, academic excellence, and social responsibility.

sections.heading: Student Formation
sections.body: The OSAFA is responsible for facilitating the formation of student organizations relevant to the general welfare and development of students. It encourages and supports students’ involvement in mandated and non-mandated organizations and supervises and monitors all activities of the University and the College Student Councils, University-based and College-based organizations.

sections.heading: Student Activities
sections.body: The Office is responsible for fostering student engagement, leadership development, advocacies, and school community building through its support of student activities. Moreover, the OSAFA is responsible for monitoring and evaluating student activities that would serve as a basis in constructing a comprehensive Master Calendar of Activities for each academic year based on the approved action plans by all colleges.

sections.heading: Scholarships and Grants
sections.body: The OSAFA provides information and assistance, facilitates the processing for the application/renewal of scholarships or grants offered by the University and external partners for deserving, academically-gifted and talented students. It is also responsible for evaluating and monitoring the progress of student grantees and scholars in their academic journey.

sections.heading: Student Discipline
sections.body: The OSAFA plays an active role in ensuring that the University core values are exhibited by all students, nurturing a culture of discipline and proper decorum. Furthermore, it ensures that offenses and violations of students are properly meted out based on the student handbook.

items.heading: Scholarships and Grants
items.body: “No one should be denied education due to poverty.” — Dr. Barbara Yap-Angeles, AUF’s Founder and First President. Hence, AUF generously offers a variety of scholarships and grants to support deserving students in their education.

sections.heading: Barbara Yap-Angeles (BYA) Scholarship (for incoming Grade 7, 11, and College Freshmen)
sections.body: This was established in honor of AUF’s Founder and First President. It is granted to Filipino honor graduates pursuing any academic program in AUF. The BYA Scholarship is granted to incoming first year college students who graduated at the top of their grade school, junior high school, or senior high school graduating/completing class according to a specific range of population. The student is entitled to a FULL SCHOLARSHIP GRANT (free tuition, miscellaneous, and laboratory fees). The scholarship may be enjoyed for four or five years provided that grades and other requirements are met.

sections.heading: Expanded Agustin P. Angeles (E-APA) Memorial Scholarship Program
sections.body: The Agustin P. Angeles Memorial Scholarship Program (APA) was established in honor of the Co-founder and First Chairman of the Board. It was originally given to college freshmen belonging to the top 10 of a high school graduating class of 100 and above. However, starting Academic Year 2023-2024, APA has been granted to freshmen in all educational levels, from basic education to post-baccalaureate programs, who satisfy the qualifications for the said scholarship grant, hence, referred to as Expanded Agustin P. Angeles Memorial Scholarship Program (E-APA). This scholarship grant is intended for financially disadvantaged but deserving students who meet the required academic and entrance test standards, as well as other eligibility requirements.

sections.heading: Academic Scholarships (for College and University Scholars)
sections.body: Academic Scholarships are extended to AUF Filipino college students who obtained the following grade requirements:
bullets: General weighted average (GWA) of not less than 95% with no grade lower than 87% in any of the enrolled courses for UNIVERSITY SCHOLARS.
General weighted average (GWA) of not less than 90% with no grade lower than 85% for COLLEGE SCHOLARS in the immediately preceding semester.

sections.heading: Activity Grants (for University Athletic Teams and University Performing Arts)
sections.body: Activity Grants are extended to students who are qualified and active members of the University Athletic Teams and of the University Performing Arts. The grant is enjoyed for as long as the student is an active member of the team or group but not more than the number of years required for the course they are pursuing. The amount of discounts for activity grants shall depend on the number of years of service as well as on the caliber, category and talents of the grantee.

sections.heading: Service Grants (for Student Aides)
sections.body: Service Grants are extended to students who are serving the University as student assistants (student aides).

sections.heading: AFP Scholarship Grant
sections.body: By virtue of P.D. 577, it is given to dependents of Military Personnel of the Armed Forces of the Philippines who died or were incapacitated in line of duty, as of September 21, 1972. It is good for 10 years from first availment and is transferable to any dependent of the deceased or incapacitated military personnel.

sections.heading: Resolution 7960 Scholarship Grant
sections.body: Resolution 7960 Scholarship Grant is given to the active members and legitimate children of the Philippine National Police (PNP), Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP) and Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) assigned in Angeles City. The resolution also includes dependent of military personnel of the Philippine Army, Navy and Philippine Air Force and retired military personnel and other uniformed personnel of Angeles City.

sections.heading: External Scholarships
sections.body: The University also offers scholarships established through collaborations with distinguished individuals, organizations, government agencies, and partner institutions that share the University’s commitment to supporting students’ education. Through these grants, qualified students receive financial assistance, incentives, or tuition discounts based on academic programs, service, affiliation, or demonstrated need. The following are some of AUF’s generous partner companies/institutions that provide scholarships and financial assistance to our students. Note: the list of qualifications and documentary requirements for external scholarships can be accessed through the institution’s official website or through its regional/local office.
bullets: Department of Science and Technology-Science Education Institute (DOST-SEI) Scholarships Programs
Commission on Higher Education (CHED) Scholarship Programs

sections.heading: Important Reminders
bullets: Scholarships and grants are subject to review and renewal every semester or term as the case may be.
A student can enjoy only one scholarship or grant during a particular semester or term.
Scholarships and grants are revocable if the scholar is found to have violated university rules and regulations, or to have joined an unauthorized student organization or activity.

offices.label: Guidance and Counseling Center
offices.tagline: Walking alongside Angeleneans in their journey of personal and academic growth.
offices.intro: The Guidance and Counseling Center of Angeles University Foundation is committed to supporting students in addressing their personal, academic, career, and social concerns while fostering the University's core values of being Mabuti (good and ethical), Magaling (competent and excellent), and May Malasakit sa Kapwa (compassionate and socially responsible). The Center aims to promote self-awareness, self-understanding, self-expression, and holistic development among students. Through individual and group counseling, developmental programs, and other guidance services, counselors work collaboratively with students to recognize their strengths, develop resilience, make informed decisions, and effectively cope with life's challenges. The Center also seeks to cultivate empathy, social awareness, responsible citizenship, and positive interpersonal relationships, inspiring students to care for others, contribute meaningfully to their communities, and embody the values of service and compassion. By nurturing students' personal, academic, career, and social development, the Guidance and Counseling Center empowers them to reach their fullest potential and emerge as competent, ethical, compassionate, and socially responsible individuals who exemplify the ideals of being Mabuti, Magaling, and May Malasakit sa Kapwa, prepared to meet the demands of higher education, work, and life.

offices.philosophy: The mission of Angeles University Foundation is the harmonious development of man for services to God and Humanity. In keeping with this mission, the Guidance and Counseling Center of the university aims at the optimum development of the human person so that he may live with dignity and integrity. The Guidance Center believes that its duty is to help the student become a knowing, loving, and responsible person, live a well-balanced life satisfying to himself and to society.
objectives: To help students identify their potentials, abilities, and interests and provide opportunities for their development and effective utilization.
To help students understand themselves better—their interests, abilities, needs, and concerns—so they can make informed decisions and appropriate adjustments.
To help students develop positive attitudes and sound moral and spiritual values.
To help students develop their ability to solve problems, communicate effectively, and build healthy relationships with others.
To help students develop effective learning skills that support their progress from one educational level to another and prepare them for future career and life goals.
To establish linkages with other units of the University and with community agencies to support and achieve the objectives of the program.
To conduct studies that will assist deans, teachers, and guidance personnel in understanding students better through the appropriate use of assessment and research data.

coreServices.title: Individual Student Planning
coreServices.description: Helps students create and follow personal, academic, and career plans through psychological testing, interviews, follow-ups, and career guidance.

coreServices.title: Guidance Instruction
coreServices.description: Provides structured activities that build life skills and support student development.

coreServices.title: Responsive Services
coreServices.description: Offers immediate support through counseling, consultation, referral, and peer facilitation (Kayantabe Peer Support Club).

coreServices.title: Management Systems
coreServices.description: Ensures services are efficiently organized and aligned with program goals.

coreServices.title: System Support
coreServices.description: Strengthens the guidance program through training, partnerships, and stakeholder collaboration.

coreServices.title: Assessment
coreServices.description: Evaluates the effectiveness of services to continually improve the program.

offices.label: University Health Services
offices.tagline: Promoting the health and well-being of every member of the AUF community.
offices.intro: The University Health Services (UHS) office is a cornerstone of student and employee health on the campus, providing an inclusive, supportive, and non-discriminatory environment where all stakeholders can have equal access to comprehensive range of medical, dental, mental health support, wellness services and other resources to promote a healthy learning and work environment without fear of bias or exclusion. With a vision of fostering a community where every student and employee thrives, the office offers both in-person and virtual appointments to accommodate diverse needs. Services include general health consultations, immunization, and mental health support among others. Emphasizing preventive care and education, the office also engages in community outreach and health promotion activities. The office is staffed with dedicated and licensed professionals including doctors, dentists, and nurses committed to delivering compassionate and confidential care to ensure the well-being of students and employees.
aims: Promotion of health through information campaigns on communicable and non-communicable diseases.
Assessment of the academic community's health status through physical and medical examinations.
Prevention of diseases through immunization, periodic monitoring of university facilities such as potability of water, pest control and sanitation.
Provision of medical and dental consultation, and management of diseases.
Facilitates wellness program activities and evaluation.

offices.label: Sports and Athletics
offices.tagline: Building champions of character and excellence on and off the field.
offices.intro: The University's Athletics Office (AO) is a dynamic hub, central to the coordination and management of the university's sports programs. This office is responsible for the planning and execution of athletic events, ensuring compliance with athletic regulations, and overseeing the maintenance of sports facilities. The office oversees the hiring of coaches and staff, schedules games and competitions, and ensures that all athletic programs operate within the set guidelines and standards. The office serves as a bridge between the university's athletic teams and the wider community, promoting sportsmanship, teamwork, and the holistic development of student-athletes.

offices.label: Culture and Arts
offices.tagline: Celebrating Filipino culture and nurturing artistic excellence among Angeleneans.
intro: The AUF Center for Culture and the Arts is tasked to help preserve the rich cultural heritage of the Kapampangans, in particular, and the Filipinos, in general, through performances of the AUF performing arts groups. It also organizes the prestigious Mr. and Ms. University Pageant and the Annual Inter-Collegiate Cultural Competitions.

The AUF Performing Arts was initially organized by Dr. Emmanuel Y. Angeles in 1963 at the former Angeles Institute of Technology in Angeles City to provide a venue for young Kapampangan artists to share and develop their talents, while pursuing college education under scholarship.
Now under the umbrella of the AUF Center for Culture and the Arts, the AUF Performing Arts boasts of five power groups.

performingArtsGroups.name: AUF Concert Chorus
performingArtsGroups.description: Organized in 1979, the AUF Concert Chorus has distinguished itself as a premiere chorale whose talent, creativity, discipline and personality have literally brought them places — including performances for Philippine Presidents in Malacañang and audiences here and abroad.

performingArtsGroups.name: AUF Dance Troupe
performingArtsGroups.description: Formed in 1973, the AUF Dance Troupe expresses the full range of Filipino artistry — from folk to modern — under the directorship of Mr. Rommel "Poklong" Guina.

performingArtsGroups.name: AUF Brass Band
performingArtsGroups.description: The very first group formed in 1963, the AUF Brass Band continues to entertain during religious, social, and cultural celebrations, today under the baton of Ms. Tiffany Chei Manaloto.

performingArtsGroups.name: AUF High School Glee Club
performingArtsGroups.description: Originally formed in 1995, the Glee Club charms audiences with youthful renditions ranging from broadway to contemporary pop. Members eventually graduate into the AUF Concert Chorus.

performingArtsGroups.name: AUF Rondalla
performingArtsGroups.description: Partners with the Dance Troupe since 1973, the AUF Rondalla wows audiences here and abroad through renditions of local and international favorites under the baton of Mr. Leovie Ruga.

offices.label: Christian and Catholic Formation Program
offices.tagline: Accompanying every Angelenean in their journey of faith and spiritual formation.
offices.intro: The Center for Christian Formation and Praxis (CCFP) is tasked to promote and sustain the Catholic character of the University through its curricular programs, community extension services, and spiritual enrichment activities. Specifically, CCFP is primarily responsible for the following programs:

programs.body: Offering of CFE and NSTP Curricula and initiating curricular and extra-curricular activities for students.
Implementation, supervision and monitoring of all University and College-based Community Extension participated by both employees and students.
Facilitation of spiritual enrichment activities including celebration of the Sacraments and related para-liturgical celebrations, Annual Faculty Retreats and Students' Recollections and Retreats.
Supervision of Mandated and Non-Mandated Religious Organizations namely, National Service Corps (Praxis-NSRC) and CYA, YFC, Oikoumene, and Campus Ministry Service Groups, respectively.
Provision of support for Adult Ministries namely, Couples for Christ, Singles for Christ, Lingkod ng Panginoon, Lector and Commentator Group, and the University Pastoral Council.
Organizing Advocacy Programs which firm up the commitment of both students and employees to the promotion of well-being of the society and the environment.

offices.closing: Overall, CCFP promotes programs and activities that are geared towards inculcation of values, deepening social awareness and responsibility, instilling volunteerism and initiative and maximizing the stakeholders' participation in the task of evangelization. Consequently, all the initiatives aim to strengthen the University Community in its faith-commitment to become authentic witnesses of God's Love.
